chunks: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) was asked: 'By what thing did you precede the children of Adam?' He said: 'I was the first one to acknowledge my Lord. Indeed, God took the Covenant of the Prophets and made them testify against themselves: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. So I was the first one to answer.'

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: Acknowledged/affirmed — in Islamic theology this term refers to the formal recognition of Lordship in the primordial covenant
key_terms.سَبَقْتَ: Precedence — spiritual rank and priority established through the primordial covenant
key_terms.مِيثَاق: Covenant/Pact — the primordial covenant of Alast taken from the Prophets (and all of humanity according to other narrations) before creation
key_terms.وُلْدَ آدَمَ: Children of Adam — all of humanity descended from the Prophet Adam (AS)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad precede all other people according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith records Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, AS) narrating that the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) was asked the reason for his precedence over all the children of Adam. The Prophet replied that he was the first to affirm his Lord's lordship during the primordial Covenant of Alast (Quran 7:172), when God gathered the souls of all Prophets and made them testify to His Lordship. This covenant, known as the 'Alam al-Dharr' or the world of spirits, establishes the pre-eternal priority of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) in acknowledging and affirming divine sovereignty, highlighting his unique spiritual station above all creation.
